data.title: Router Buffer Dimensioning under Poisson
data.statement:
A network router aggregates traffic from multiple users. Due to the bursty nature of network traffic, packet arrivals fluctuate over time and are modeled using a Poisson process.

The router has limited transmission capacity and a finite buffer. Your task is to determine the minimum buffer size required to ensure that the probability of packet loss remains below a given threshold.

To evaluate rare overload events, a Chernoff bound approximation is used instead of exact probability computation.
data.inputDescription:
The input contains four values:

n: number of users in the network 
lambda_u: average packet generation rate per user 
C: router transmission capacity per time slot
L: maximum acceptable packet loss probability

All values are given in a single line.
data.outputDescription: The output is a single integer representing the minimum buffer size B such that the packet loss probability is less than or equal to L.

Goal

A network router aggregates traffic from multiple users. Due to the bursty nature of network traffic, packet arrivals fluctuate over time and are modeled using a Poisson process.

The router has limited transmission capacity and a finite buffer. Your task is to determine the minimum buffer size required to ensure that the probability of packet loss remains below a given threshold.

To evaluate rare overload events, a Chernoff bound approximation is used instead of exact probability computation.
Input
The input contains four values:

n: number of users in the network
lambda_u: average packet generation rate per user
C: router transmission capacity per time slot
L: maximum acceptable packet loss probability

All values are given in a single line.
Output
The output is a single integer representing the minimum buffer size B such that the packet loss probability is less than or equal to L.
Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
0 < lambdaUSER < 10
1 ≤ C ≤ 1000
0 < L < 1
Example
Input
1 0.5 2 0.5
Output
0
